# Understand your readiness score on Apple Watch

In the Readiness app on Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4, you can view a readiness score and a classification that helps you understand your capacity to take on activities during the day.

## **Readiness score classifications**

Your readiness score ranges from 0-10:

- **Go for it:**8–10
- **Ready:**5–7
- **Pace Yourself:**2–4
- **Recover:**0–1

![Apple Watch showing a readiness score of 7.](https://cdsassets.apple.com/live/7WUAS350/images/apple-watch/watchos-27-series-12-readiness-score-7-ready.png)

## If you don't receive a readiness score

Make sure you've done the following:

- Entered your height, weight, and age [under your Health Details](https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/iph5f0e22170/ios).
- Set up [Activity](https://support.apple.com/guide/watch/apd3bf6d85a6/watchos).
- Set up [overnight vitals](https://support.apple.com/en-us/120142), and worn your watch while sleeping for at least 7 nights.
- Set up and enabled [Sleep](https://support.apple.com/en-us/108906), and slept with your watch last night.

## **Learn how your readiness score is calculated**

Your Activity data, daytime and overnight vitals, and sleep data factor into your overall readiness score.

- **Activity:**Activity from both today and your recent history can impact your readiness score. Active calories, workout effort ratings, and Training Load data are all used to calculate the score. Increased activity in general can reduce your score, while steady or reduced activity raises it. Additionally, you might see your score go down during the day after a workout or activity.
- **Vitals:** Readiness considers the status of your daytime and overnight metrics from the Vitals app. When your vitals indicate you're Notably or Slightly off, your score is reduced. When all of your metrics are Typical or Favorable, your score is raised. Higher-than-usual heart rate variability (HRV) can lead to Favorable vitals and a high readiness score.
- **Sleep:** Your sleep score from the previous night and your recent history can impact your readiness score. A low sleep score from poor-quality or inconsistent sleep can reduce your readiness score, while a high sleep score, or an improved sleep score, can raise your readiness score.

Readiness does not account for all health factors such as existing conditions or medications, and should not be solely relied on to determine whether it is safe to exercise. Consider discontinuing workouts or seeking medical attention if you experience concerning symptoms. Readiness is a general wellness feature and should not be used as a substitute for professional medical judgment.

# How to unlock Apple’s new dynamic Readiness Score on your Apple Watch

By Dan Bracaglia (Senior Writer, Fitness & Wearables), Tom's Guide. Published 2026-10-22.

The Apple Watch finally has a dynamic Readiness Score. Based on a scale from zero to ten, the score takes into account your recent sleep quality, physical activity, and vital trends.

Unlocking your dynamic Readiness Score on Apple Watch is fairly straightforward, though you will need to wear the device for seven nights to see your first one.

Apple's Readiness Score is just one of the cool, new features found in the [best Apple Watch](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-apple-watch) models in 2026. Others include support for a vastly improved [AI-powered Siri](https://www.tomsguide.com/wellness/smartwatches/how-to-enable-siri-ai-on-your-apple-watch), real-time [dynamic step count data](https://www.tomsguide.com/wellness/smartwatches/how-to-add-apples-new-dynamic-step-count-widget-to-your-apple-watch), an impressively comprehensive at-home [wellness assessment](https://www.tomsguide.com/wellness/smartwatches/i-tried-apples-new-at-home-wellness-assessment-in-ios-27-and-gained-valuable-insights-into-my-flexibility-and-balance), and [Live Rewind](https://www.tomsguide.com/wellness/smartwatches/im-a-smartwatch-reviewer-this-is-the-new-apple-watch-12-feature-im-most-excited-for), an AI tool that transcribes live audio around you.

Of course, I've already covered all of the above at length; here's how to unlock Apple's new dynamic Readiness Score on your Apple Watch in four easy steps.

## How to unlock the Readiness Score on your Apple Watch

1. **Make sure you have a compatible Apple Watch model**
2. **Enter your height, weight, and age in the Apple Fitness app**
3. **Wear your Apple Watch to bed for seven consecutive nights; ensure you get at least four hours of sleep per night**
4. **After seven nights logged, open the Readiness app on your Apple Watch to see your dynamic score**

*Read on to see full illustrated instructions for each step.*

### 1. Make sure you have a compatible Apple Watch model

![Close-up of the Apple Watch 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 on a user's wrist](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/HuFVW7DSMUng84qvE57MVT.jpg)

Before we dive into the Readiness Score setup process, **first make sure you have a compatible Apple Watch model.**Unfortunately, only those with Apple's latest S11 chip have access to the feature for now. That list includes only the [Apple Watch Series 12](https://www.tomsguide.com/wellness/smartwatches/apple-watch-series-12-review) and [Apple Watch Ultra 4](https://www.tomsguide.com/wellness/smartwatches/apple-watch-ultra-4-review), though other models may be added down the road.

### 2. Enter your height, weight, and age in the Apple Fitness app

![Screenshot from the health details section of the Apple Fitness app](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/eTc5BcBcCFgoWKunVFZdzX.jpg)

Next, **open the Fitness app on your companion iPhone, tap "Summary," and then tap the icon in the top-right corner of the screen**; it should either be a small photo of you or your initials. Next, **scroll down and tap "Health Details," and enter your age, weight, and height.**

You'll also want to**ensure that you have daily activity, vitals, and**[**sleep tracking**](https://www.tomsguide.com/wellness/smartwatches/watchos-26-heres-how-to-enable-your-apple-watchs-sleep-score)**turned on** (they should be on by default). **Double-check by opening each app on your Apple Watch**; if tracking is on, you'll see recent data. If it's not, you'll be prompted to turn it on.

### 3. Wear your Apple Watch to bed for seven consecutive nights

![Close-up of the Apple Watch 12 on a user's wrist with a recent sleep report shown on the screen](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/eqXrqiAqxcpcuoVfQ7FZ3f.jpg)

With all your health details entered, the only thing you'll need to do to generate your first Readiness Score is**wear your Apple Watch for seven consecutive nights, ensuring you get at least four hours of sleep per night.** You'll also want to wear it during the day to ensure accurate activity data.

### 4. Open the Readiness app on your Apple Watch to see your dynamic score

![Close-up of the Apple Watch Series 12 on a user's wrist at the Cupertino launch event on September 10, 2026](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/m4WYYb9cwZa49jDrhG22RE.jpg)

After seven nights, your first Readiness Score should be, well, ready! To view it, **open the new Readiness app on your Apple Watch**. It's a blue circle with a pink and green scale in it (shown in the bottom left of the image above).

![Close-up of the Apple Watch 12 home screen; the daily Readiness Score as one of several widgets shown](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/u4rBKarcnhBMVXdeQU9Jxn.jpg)

(Image credit: Tom's Guide)

Readiness Scores break down into four categories: "Recover" (0-1), "Pace Yourself" (2-4), "Ready" (5-7), and "Go for it" (8-10).

Keep in mind, after your initial Readiness Score is generated, it will dynamically update throughout the day as you go about your business. Workouts, movement, naps, and heart rate can all have an impact on your real-time score.

And for easy viewing, there's even a Readiness Score widget you can add to your watch's home screen, right alongside the new [Siri AI](https://www.tomsguide.com/wellness/smartwatches/how-to-enable-siri-ai-on-your-apple-watch) and [dynamic step count](https://www.tomsguide.com/wellness/smartwatches/how-to-add-apples-new-dynamic-step-count-widget-to-your-apple-watch) widgets.

# Apple Watch Readiness Score on Series 10, 11 and Ultra 3

Find out which Apple Watch models get Apple's Readiness score, why yours may not show one, and how to get a readiness read on Series 10, 11 or Ultra 3.

**Apple's Readiness score runs only on Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, so a Series 10, 11, Ultra 2 or Ultra 3 won't show one.** You can still get a daily readiness read on those watches. [Body Insights](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/body-insights-for-apple-watch/id6467108273) reads the HRV, resting heart rate and sleep your watch already records, and gives you a plain answer each morning.

Apple launched Readiness in September with the new watches. It rates your day from 0 to 10 and adds one of four labels. Many owners of last year's watches went looking for the app and couldn't find it. Here's why, and what to use instead.

## Which Apple Watch models get Readiness?

Apple ties Readiness to the new Health Sensing System in Series 12 and Ultra 4, according to [Apple's September announcement](https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/09/apple-advances-health-and-fitness-capabilities-using-apple-intelligence/). That system measures heart rate and HRV more often than earlier watches.

| Apple Watch | Apple Readiness app | Daily readiness in Body Insights |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Series 12, Ultra 4 | Yes | Yes |
| Series 11, Ultra 3 | No | Yes |
| Series 10, Ultra 2 | No | Yes |
| Apple Watch SE | No | Yes |

Older models running watchOS 27 don't get the Readiness app, because it relies on those new sensors.

## Why your Readiness score isn't showing

If you have a Series 12 or Ultra 4 and see no score, Apple lists four things to check in its [readiness guide](https://support.apple.com/en-us/128112):

1. Enter your height, weight, and age in your Health Details.
2. Set up Activity.
3. Set up overnight vitals, and wear your watch to sleep for at least 7 nights.
4. Set up Sleep, and wear your watch to bed last night.

The 7-night rule catches most new owners. A watch bought this week won't give a score until next week.

## Why is your readiness score low?

Apple's score reads three things: activity, vitals, and sleep. Each can pull it down.

- **Activity:** more activity than usual lowers the score. A hard workout can drop it later the same day.
- **Vitals:** if your overnight or daytime vitals are Slightly off or Notably off, the score goes down.
- **Sleep:** a low sleep score from short or uneven sleep lowers it.

Each label covers a fixed range. Recover is 0 to 1, Pace Yourself is 2 to 4, Ready is 5 to 7, and Go For It is 8 to 10. So a 4 after a big weekend means "pace yourself," not "something is wrong."

## Get a daily readiness read on Series 10, 11 and Ultra 3

Body Insights gives older watches a morning answer to the same question. Its Daily Coach reads what your Apple Watch recorded overnight: HRV, resting heart rate, sleep, and wrist temperature. It compares them with your own baseline, not an athlete's.

Then it gives you one of four words: Rest, Light, Moderate, or Push. One or two sentences explain why. A morning might say, "Today, take it slow. Your overnight recovery was lighter than usual." If you want a number, the 0 to 100 score sits underneath.

Here's how that plays out. Say you ran on Saturday and slept badly on Sunday. On Monday your HRV is below your baseline and your resting heart rate is up. Body Insights tells you to keep the day light. You move the gym session to Tuesday.

Its readiness check also weighs your training load, comparing recent strain with your longer-term fitness. If you wear a CGM such as Stelo, Dexcom, or Libre, it adds overnight glucose to the morning read. Without one, the other signals carry the check.

## Apple Readiness vs Body Insights

|  | Apple Readiness | Body Insights |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Watches | Series 12 and Ultra 4 | Any Apple Watch that records to Apple Health |
| Answer | 0 to 10 score with four labels | Rest, Light, Moderate or Push, plus a 0 to 100 score |
| Inputs | Activity, vitals, sleep score. | Heart data, sleep, wrist temperature, training load, and optional CGM glucose. |
| Updates | Through the day | Each morning |
| Price | Built in | Free download |

If you own a Series 12 or Ultra 4, use both. Apple's score updates through the day. Body Insights adds your own baseline and plain advice for variable energy.

## Frequently asked questions about Apple Watch Readiness

### Does Apple Watch Ultra 3 have a Readiness score?

Apple Watch Ultra 3 does not get Apple's Readiness score. Readiness requires Series 12 or Ultra 4.

### Why is Readiness missing on a new Series 12 or Ultra 4?

Series 12 and Ultra 4 need your height, weight, and age, Activity set up, Sleep set up, and at least 7 nights of overnight wear before the first score.

### How can Series 10, 11, SE, or Ultra 3 get a daily readiness read?

Body Insights reads HRV, resting heart rate, and sleep already in Apple Health and gives a morning readiness read on Series 10, Series 11, SE, Ultra 2, and Ultra 3.

[Download Body Insights](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/body-insights-for-apple-watch/id6467108273) and check tomorrow morning's read before you plan your workout.
